headline: High: Plandex can write and egress by default, so pairing it with a non-runnable course repo creates dangerous default-side effects and possible instruction confusion.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A has no runtime I/O surfaces and is not runnable, so it cannot directly ingest B's outputs. B can read/write files and use stdin/stdout, so if an operator manually copies A-derived text into B, prompt injection is possible, but the bridge is manual rather than default.
conditions: IF an operator copies A-generated text into B's prompt or files
IF B is configured to treat copied course content as instructions
mitigations: Keep A and B in separate terminals
Paste only vetted excerpts into B
Prefix copied A content as data, not instructions
Disable auto-apply in B
Use a review checklist before executing B outputs

B_data_leakage.rationale: A touches no declared sensitive data and has no egress. B can read the filesystem and has broad network egress, but the pair does not show a shared workspace or sensitive data class. Leakage risk is therefore limited to accidental exposure of ordinary files if the operator places them in B's project directory.
conditions: IF the operator places sensitive files inside B's project directory
IF B is given access to files that A produced or referenced
mitigations: Do not mount sensitive directories into B
Use a throwaway workspace for B
Review B's file access before running
Keep A materials outside B's project directory
Rotate any secrets copied into the workspace

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A has no write or network capabilities, while B can write the filesystem, modify git state, and spawn subprocesses. There is no direct overlap from A, but if both are pointed at the same repo or directory, B can overwrite A's materials or git state. Uncertainty about A's filesystem surface is not enough to downgrade.
conditions: IF A and B are pointed at the same working directory
IF B auto-applies changes while another instance is active
mitigations: Use separate directories for A and B
Avoid concurrent B sessions on the same repo
Commit or stash before running B
Disable auto-apply in B
Add a manual diff review step

D_cascading_error.rationale: A is a course repo and B is a coding agent with review-then-apply behavior. If A's content is copied into B as guidance, B may treat it as authoritative and act on it without verification. B's sandbox reduces but does not eliminate downstream mistakes, so the pathway exists but is not inherently catastrophic.
conditions: IF A's text is used as an input spec for B
IF B is run in auto-apply mode or without human review
mitigations: Require human review before apply
Ask B to cite sources for claims
Use A only as reference material
Turn off auto-apply
Validate B's proposed commands in a dry run

E_compliance.rationale: No compliance-sensitive data class, residency mismatch, or regulated retention policy is declared for A, and B only declares source code plus model-provider API keys. With the available profiles, there is no documented compliance breach pathway to assess.
conditions: IF regulated data such as PHI or EU PII is introduced into either agent
IF a deployment policy imposes residency or retention constraints not shown here
mitigations: Do not place regulated data in either agent
Confirm retention settings before use
Keep API keys out of shared workspaces
Use a separate compliant environment for regulated data
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for data residency
